title: A Note For Yourself
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = A Note For Yourself | Image = Event-SelfNote.png }} {{E|A Note For Yourself}} is an [[Event]] encountered in all [[Acts]]. == Options == {{Frame|Take and Give}} {{TS|positive||Receive and Store a Card}} * Receive a card that you had stored previously, and store a card in your deck in return. ** The first time the player encounters this event in their save file, it will have {{C|Iron Wave}} stored. {{Frame|Ignore}} Nothing happens.

You are then given the option to {{Frame|Leave}}. == Dialogue ==
You spot a loose brick within a pillar that catches your eye.
You find a folded note and a {{TS|gold||card}} inside. It reads,
"The Heart awaits"

This is your handwriting.

{{Frame|Take and Give}}
Choose a Card to Store.
Prior to {{Frame|Leave}}
"What is going on?"
== Gameplay Notes == * This event can store a card between runs, and allows the player to obtain a card from a different character. * On {{Asc|14}} or lower, the player must have beaten that Ascension level on the chosen character in order to encounter this event. * On {{Asc|15}} or higher, this event cannot be encountered. * Playing the [[Daily Climb]] also disables this event. * If you store an upgraded card, it remains upgraded when found on another run. ** {{C|Searing Blow}} retains its upgrade level when it was stored. * Retrieving a card is considered adding a card to your deck, and will trigger relics such as {{R|Molten Egg}}, {{R|Toxic Egg}}, {{R|Frozen Egg}}, and {{R|Ceramic Fish}}. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Ancient Writing
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Ancient Writing | Image = Event-AncientWriting.png }} {{E|Ancient Writing}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. == Options == {{Frame|Elegance}} {{TS|positive||Remove a card from your deck.}}

{{Frame|Simplicity}} {{TS|positive||[[Upgrade]] all Strikes and Defends.}} * Only includes {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} cards. == Dialogue ==
Scaling the city, you notice a wall covered in the writing of {{TS|gold|up|Ancients.}} As you try to wrap your head around what the puzzling symbols and glyphs could mean, the writing begins to {{TS|blue|up|glow.}}
Suddenly, the message becomes clear...


{{Frame|Elegance}}
The answer was elegance.
Of course.
{{Frame|Simplicity}}
The truth is always simple.
== Trivia == * The internal name of this event is Back_to_Basics. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 50: The Final Act''' ** Fixed softlock caused if you can't remove cards in: Back to Basics, Cleric, and Living Wall events. * '''Weekly Patch 17: Patched in the Face''' ** Ascender's Bane can no longer be removed by Back to Basics event. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Augmenter
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Augmenter | Image = Event-Augmenter.png }} {{Small Relic Infobox|Mutagenic Strength}} {{Small Card Infobox|J.A.X.}} {{E|Augmenter}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. This Event is the only way to obtain {{C|J.A.X.}} and {{R|Mutagenic Strength}}. == Options == {{Frame|Test J.A.X.}} {{TS|positive||Get JAXXED.}} * Adds {{C|J.A.X.}} to the player's deck.
{{Frame|Become Test Subject}} {{TS|positive||[[Transform]] 2 cards.}} * Read more on Transform rules [[Transform#Rules|here]].
{{Frame|Ingest Mutagens}} {{TS|positive|| Obtain a special relic.}} * Rewards the player with {{R|Mutagenic Strength}}. == Dialogue ==
A man with an eyepatch and a devilish grin strides up to you.
"Hey there, stranger. Interested in advancing science? I can make you stronger than any training or blessing. You're gonna need it if you're one of those heroes with a death wish."

{{TS||up|"Whad'ya say?"}}


{{Frame|Test J.A.X.}}
{{TS||up|"Excellent."}}
The man hands over a dangerous looking syringe filled with a {{TS|blue|up|glowing liquid}} before skulking off into a shadowy alleyway.
{{Frame|Become Test Subject}}
{{TS||up|"Marvelous."}}
You quaff the mysterious substance. Immediately, you are invigorated and feel your muscle fibers {{TS||shake|twitch.}}
{{Frame|Ingest Mutagens}}
{{TS||up|"Superb."}}
The man injects you with three unknown substances and pulls out a notepad. As you begin to feel light-headed, he starts to frantically write down notes.
Losing track of time completely, by the time you regain your senses, the shady character has disappeared.
== Trivia == * Augmenter was originally called "J.A.X. Dealer". It was renamed because, early into Slay the Spire's development, {{E|Pleading Vagrant}} previously accepted {{C|J.A.X.}} from the J.A.X. Dealer but was reworked to accept 85 [[Gold]] instead. Following the change, the old name no longer made sense and had to also be changed. It could have also been changed due to the negative connotations of the word "dealer". * Internally called Drug_Dealer. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion''' ** Minor text cleanup for Augmenter event. ** Typo fix in Augmenter event. * '''Weekly Patch 46: Adrenaline''' ** Fixed punctuation in Augmenter event. * '''Weekly Patch 44: Chrysalis''' ** Augmenter event transform option now allows choosing 2 cards to Transform instead of selecting 3 at random. * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** Augmenter event no longer incorrectly upgrades transformed cards. ** Augmenter event will no longer give out duplicate relics on Endless mode. * '''Weekly Patch 39: We Meet Again!''' ** J.A.X Dealer event reworked. ** J.A.X. Dealer event renamed -> Augmenter. * '''Weekly Patch 21: Channel Lightning''' ** J.A.X. Dealer event's cost of J.A.X. updated 100 -> 77 Gold. * '''Weekly Patch 4: Full speed ahead!''' ** Incorrectly using wavy text in JAX event fixed. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Big Fish
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Big Fish | Image = Event-BigFish.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Regret}} {{E|Big Fish}} is an event found exclusively in [[Act 1]]. == Options == {{Frame|Banana}} {{TS|positive||Heal 1/3 of your max HP.}} * If the player's HP is not divisble by 3, the HP gain is rounded down.
{{Frame|Donut}} {{TS|positive||Max HP +5.}} * Like all HP gain, the extra hit points are healed when you get them.
{{Frame|Box}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a [[Relic]].}} {{TS|negative||Become Cursed - {{C|Regret}}.}} * The {{QueryLink|Relics||Relic}} is a randomly selected {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common}}, {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}}, or {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare}} Relic.
You are then given the option to {{Frame|Leave}}. == Dialogue ==
As you make your way down a long corridor you see a {{TS|gold||banana}}, a {{TS|gold||donut}}, and a {{TS|gold||box}} {{TS||up|floating}} about. No... upon closer inspection they are tied to strings coming from holes in the ceiling. There is a quiet {{TS||shake|cackling}} from above as you approach the objects. What do you do?

{{Frame|Banana}}
You eat the {{TS|gold||banana}}. It is nutritious and slightly {{TS|blue||magical}}, healing you.
{{Frame|Donut}}
You eat the {{TS|gold||donut}}. It really hits the spot! Your Max HP increases.
{{Frame|Box}}
You grab the box. Inside you find a {{TS|gold||relic!}}
However, you really craved the donut...
You are filled with {{TS||up|sadness,}} but mostly regret.
{{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Bonfire Spirits
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Bonfire Spirits | Image = Event-BonfireSpirits.png }} {{Small Relic Infobox|Spirit Poop}} {{E|Bonfire Spirits}} is a shrine [[Event]] found in all [[Acts]]. Shrine events appear less frequently than other events. == Options == {{Frame|Offer}} Receive a reward based on the offer. * Offer a card in your deck to remove. The reward you receive depends on the rarity of the card you give. == Dialogue ==
You happen upon what looks like a group of {{TS|purple||purple fire spirits}} {{TS||up|dancing}} around a large bonfire. Before selecting {{Frame|Offer}}
The spirits toss small bones and fragments into the fire, which {{TS||up|brilliantly erupts}} each time.
As you approach, the spirits all turn to you, expectantly...
{{Frame|Offer}}
You toss an offering into the bonfire. When offering a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} card
Nothing happens...
The spirits seem to be ignoring you now. Disappointing...
When offering a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}} card
The flames grow slightly brighter.
The spirits continue dancing. You feel slightly warmer from their presence..
You {{TS|green||heal}} {{TS|blue||5}} HP.
When offering an {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} card
The flames erupt, growing significantly stronger!
The spirits dance around you excitedly, filling you with a {{TS||up|sense of warmth.}}
You are {{TS|green||healed}} to full HP.
When offering a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} card
The flames {{TS||shake|burst}}, nearly knocking you off your feet, as the fire {{TS||shake|doubles}} in strength.
The spirits dance around you excitedly before {{TS||up|merging into your form,}} filling you with warmth and strength.
Your Max HP increases by {{TS|blue||10}} and you are {{TS|green||healed}} to full HP.
When offering a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}
However, the spirits aren't happy you offered a {{TS|purple||Curse...}}
The card fizzles a meek black smoke. You receive a... {{TS|purple|up|something}} in return.
(Gives {{R|Spirit Poop}})
== Notes == * This event treats {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} cards as a lower rarity than {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}}. * Obtaining {{R|Spirit Poop}} adds the '''Poopy''' [[Score]] bonus which lowers your total score by one. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Council of Ghosts
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Council of Ghosts | Image = Event-Ghosts.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Apparition}} {{E|Council of Ghosts}} is an event found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Accept}} {{TS|positive||Receive 5}} {{Asc|15|(3)}} {{C|Apparition|Apparitions}}. {{TS|negative||Lose X Max HP.}} * X is equal to 50% of the player's Max HP, rounded up. {{Frame|Refuse}} Nothing happens.

You are then given the option to {{Frame|Leave}}. == Dialogue ==
As you continue your ascent, {{TS|purple|up|thick black smoke}} begins to billow out of the ground and walls around you, coalescing into three masked forms that start to speak.
{{TS||up|"Another puppet of }} {{TS|gold|up|Neow}} {{TS||up| I think."}}
{{TS|red|shake|"AGREED! SHE ALWAYS MAKES THE FUNNEST TOYS!"}} You notice an over-sized grin as the third addresses you. "Ignore the others... Would you like a taste of our {{TS|gold|up|power?"}}
{{Frame|Accept}}
{{TS|gold||"Excellent!"}} As the ghostly shape speaks, you notice its large mouth opening wider and wider. {{TS|purple|up|Thick black smoke}} spews forth and envelops the room. You cannot see or breathe... Just before you lose consciousness, the sensation stops. Whatever those things were, they are gone now. You continue on, feeling rather {{TS|blue||hollow.}}
{{Frame|Refuse}}
"How disappointing..."
{{TS||up|"You will join us sooner or later."}}
{{TS|red|shake|"HA HA HA HAHAHA!"}} The shapes fade away, leaving only the unnerving laughter ringing in your ears.
== Trivia == * This event is internally called Ghosts. * {{C|Apparition}} is internally called Ghostly. * One of the few events that directly refer to [[Neow]], this event reveals she is female. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Cursed Tome
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Cursed Tome | Image = Event-CursedTome.png }} {{Small Relic Infobox|Enchiridion}} {{Small Relic Infobox|Nilry's Codex}} {{Small Relic Infobox|Necronomicon}} {{E|Cursed Tome}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. == Options == {{Frame|Read}}
{{Frame|Continue}} {{TS|negative||Lose 1 HP.}}
{{Frame|Continue}} {{TS|negative||Lose 2 HP.}}
{{Frame|Continue}} {{TS|negative||Lose 3 HP.}}
{{Frame|Take}} {{TS|positive||Obtain the book.}} {{TS|negative||Lose 10}} {{asc|15|(15)}} {{TS|negative||HP.}} * The book may be {{R|Enchiridion}}, {{R|Nilry's Codex}}, or {{R|Necronomicon}}. The player does not know which book they will get until after they choose {{Frame|Take}} and lose their HP.
{{Frame|Stop}} {{TS|negative||Lose 3 HP.}}
{{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. === Practical Options === Because the player can choose to leave the event immediately and lose 0 HP instead of selecting {{Frame|Continue}} 3 times and then backing out with {{Frame|Stop}} while losing a total of 9 HP, there are really only 2 practical ways to navigate the event. The player can either commit to all the HP loss and obtain the book, or leave immediately to do nothing. For simplicity, the event's options can be thought of in this way instead: * {{Frame|Read}}, then all 3 {{Frame|Continue}}, and finally {{Frame|Take}} {{TS|positive||Obtain the book.}} {{TS|negative||Lose 16}} {{asc|15|(21)}} {{TS|negative||HP.}} * {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
In an abandoned temple, you find a giant book, open, riddled with {{TS|purple|shake|cryptic writings.}}
As you try to interpret the elaborate script, it begins to {{TS|blue|up|shift}} and {{TS|blue|up|morph}} into writing you are familiar with.

{{Frame|Read}}
Odd. The book seems to be about an {{TS|gold||Ancient}} named {{TS|gold||Neow.}}
This piques your interest, but you have a general feeling of {{TS|purple|up|malaise.}}
{{Frame|Continue}}
The Ancient of Resurrection, {{TS|gold||Neow,}} was exiled to the bottom of the Spire.
You feel compelled to read more, but your body begins to {{TS|negative|up|ache.}}
{{Frame|Continue}}
Seeking vengeance, {{TS|gold||Neow}} blesses outsiders, using them for her own purposes.
You are starting to feel very {{TS|negative|up|weak and tired...}}
{{Frame|Continue}}
Those resurrected by {{TS|gold||Neow}} remember only fragments of their past selves, cursed to fight for eternity.
As you near the final page, your {{TS|negative|shake|old wounds begin to reopen!}}
{{Frame|Take}}
Upon finishing the tome, you decide to take it with you. With proof in hand, will you retain your memories?
{{Frame|Stop}}
With incredible strain and willpower, you resist the trance of the tome and {{TS||shake|SLAM}} it shut.
You turn and exit the temple, feeling {{TS|blue|up|drained...}}
{{Frame|Leave}}
You exit, feeling a {{TS|purple|up|dark energy emanating}} from the book on the pedestal.
== Notes == * {{R|Tungsten Rod}} will reduce the HP lost for each instance of damage from the event's options. If the player selects {{Frame|Continue}} 3 times and then {{Frame|Take}}, {{R|Tungsten Rod}} reduces the total HP lost by 4 for a total of 12 {{Asc|15|(17)}} HP lost instead of 16 {{Asc|15|(21)}}. ** If the player selects {{Frame|Stop}} instead of {{Frame|Take}}, {{R|Tungsten Rod}} reduces the total HP lost to 5 instead of 9. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Adding page turn SFX to Cursed Tome event. * '''Weekly Patch 17: Patched in the Face''' ** Seeds utilized for several events for consistent outcomes: Accursed Blacksmith, Cursed Tome, Scrap Ooze, N'loth. * '''Weekly Patch 16: Back to Work''' ** Cursed Tome Event now uses reward screen for the earned book relic (optional pickup). {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Dead Adventurer
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Dead Adventurer | Image = Event-DeadAdventurer.png }} {{E|Dead Adventurer}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 1]]. == Options == {{Frame|Search}} {{TS|positive||Find Loot.}} {{TS|negative||25%}} {{Asc|15|(35%)}}{{TS|negative||: monster returns.}} * Each {{Frame|Search}} attempt will either cause an [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Act 1 Elite]] to return and fight the player, or yield one of the following rewards: ** 30 [[Gold]] ** A random [[Relic]] ** Nothing * Each reward only occurs once - if the player's first search found nothing and the second search found the [[Relic]], the third search will either reward 30 [[Gold]] or start a battle. * Each reward that is acquired before fighting the [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]] will be removed from its combat rewards if the player eventually does fight the [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]] and defeats it. ** For example, if the player's first {{Frame|Search}} is a [[Relic]], the [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]] will not drop a [[Relic]] when it is defeated. ** This is also the reason why this specific [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]] fight can drop 30 extra [[Gold]] compared to a normal [[Elite]]; because the 30 [[Gold]] {{Frame|Search}} reward is added to the normal [[Gold]] reward of defeating an [[Elite]]. * Each subsequent {{Frame|Search}} increases the chance to encounter an [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]] by 25%. * If the player manages to successfully {{Frame|Search}} three times without encountering an [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]], the event will end with a short dialogue detailing the success. * For the second and third searches (assuming the player is not ambushed), {{Frame|Search}} will be called {{Frame|Continue}} instead. Its behavior and description are unchanged.

You come across a {{TS|negative||dead adventurer}} on the floor.
His {{TS|blue||pants}} have been stolen! Also, (phrasing depends on the Elite).
Though his {{TS|gold||possessions are still intact,}} you're in no mind to find out what happened here...

It also immediately debuffs the player with its {{Int|Lagavulin|Siphon Soul}} on the first turn of the fight.
{{Frame|Search}} (and {{Frame|Continue}} for the second and third searches)
If the player finds [[Gold]]:

Continue searching?

If the player finds a [[Relic]]:

Continue searching?
The player is able to {{Frame|Continue}} searching with a +25% chance for the monster to return, or {{Frame|Leave}} and end the event.
If the player finds nothing:
Hmm, couldn't find anything...
Continue searching?
The player is able to {{Frame|Continue}} searching with a +25% chance for the monster to return, or {{Frame|Leave}} and end the event.
If the player is ambushed by the [[Elites#Act 1 Elites|Elite]]:
While searching the adventurer you are caught off guard!

If this is the third successful Search in a row:

title: Events
wikitext:
{{#setmainimage:Map-Event.png|quiet}} {{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Ambox | color = var(--highlight-color-watcher) | icon = EventClear.png | message = ''This is information about '''Events''' in Slay the Spire. A full searchable list can be found at [[Events List]].'' }} [[Category:ToUpdate]] Events are unique encounters that present the player with a scenario and asks them to make a choice on how they wish to handle that scenario. These scenarios can involve running into various denizens of the Spire (both [[We Meet Again!|helpful]] and [[Masked Bandits|harmful]]), [[Golden Idol (Event)|triggering traps]], finding [[Upgrade Shrine|shrines]] and [[Forgotten Altar|altars]], [[Sensory Stone|wandering into something strange]], and much more. Events are only encountered in [[Map Locations#Unknown|Unknown floors]]. Each Act has a set of events that can only occur in that Act, but there are also events which can occur in two or three Acts. No events can occur in [[Acts#Act 4: The Ending|Act 4]] as there are no [[Map Locations#Unknown|unknown floors]] to travel to. Starting from {{Asc|15|Ascension}}, some events have less positive outcomes and/or more severe consequences. For example: more HP lost, less gold rewarded, higher prices, or a higher likelihood of being {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Cursed}}. == Encountering Events == Events are not the only type of room that can be encountered in [[Map Locations#Unknown|unknown floors]]. Whenever the player enters an unknown floor, there is a high chance that they will encounter an [[Event]] and a set of much lower chances that they encounter a [[Monsters|Monster]], [[Shop]], or [[Map Locations#Treasure Room|Treasure Room]]. Each room type has a different chance of being encountered, which the game determines randomly when entering the unknown floor. Many events have a set of criteria that must be met in order for them to be encountered. All of an event's criteria must be met for it to be eligible. Some example criteria are: * Being in a specific Act (e.g. {{E|Golden Idol}} is exclusive to Act 1) * Being under or above a specific floor (e.g. {{E|Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms}} can only be encountered within Act 1 on floor 7 or above) * Having enough [[Gold]] to afford at least one of the event's options (e.g. {{E|The Cleric}} requires at least 35 [[Gold]]) * Having a specific amount of HP remaining (e.g. {{E|Knowing Skull}} requires at least 13 HP, while {{E|The Moai Head}} requires HP to be at or below 50%) * ... and many more. Some events have very unique and specific criteria (e.g. {{E|N'loth}} requires at least 2 [[Relics]], and {{E|The Divine Fountain}} requires a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}) If the game determines that an unknown floor should be an event, there is a high chance that it will be an [[#Act Event|Act Event]] and a lower chance that it will be one of the much rarer [[#Shrine Events|Shrine Events]]. If the event should be one of the rarer [[#Shrine Events|Shrine Events]], the game will combine the eligible [[#Shrines|Shrine]] and [[#One-Time Event|One-Time Event]] pools and then pick a random event from that combined pool. == Types of Events == While there is no in-game distinction between event types, it can be useful to understand the internal details because different event types have different rules on how they can be encountered. Internally, there are 3 types of events: [[#Act Events|Act Events]], [[#Shrines|Shrines]], and [[#One-Time Events|One-Time Events]]. ''Note:'' There is an "unofficial" event type which the Slay the Spire community calls [[#Shrine Events|"Shrine Events"]]. This is different from (but related to) [[#Shrines|Shrines]]. The language used on this page is '''''very careful''''' to correctly refer to "Shrines" or "Shrine Events" depending on the context, as these are two separate terms that '''do not mean the same thing''' but are closely related and easy to mix up. Read those sections for more information. See the table below for a quick summary of the differences between event types. {| class="wikitable" |+Event Type Summary !Event Type !Encounter Frequency !Restricted to a
Specific Act? !Repeatable? !Sometimes Referred to as a
"[[Events#Shrine Events|Shrine Event]]" by the Community? |- |'''[[Events#Act Events|Act Event]]''' |Common |Yes |No |No |- |'''[[Events#Shrines|Shrine]]''' |Rare |No |Yes, after Act transition |Yes |- |'''[[Events#One-Time Events|One-Time Event]]''' |Rare |Varies |No |Yes |} === Act Events === Internally, these are simply called Events. Act events can be considered as the baseline "normal events". They can all only be encountered in a specific Act, and can each only be encountered once. For example, {{E|Big Fish}} is an event that is exclusive to Act 1. Once the player encounters it in Act 1 they will not see that event again for the remainder of Act 1 (and by extension, the rest of the run). If they do not see {{E|Big Fish}} during Act 1, they have missed their chance to encounter it and it is now impossible to see the event on that run. For a list of all Act Events, see the {{QueryLink|Events||Events List}} filtered to a particular Act ({{QueryLink|Events|act:1&shrine:No|Act 1 Events}} or {{QueryLink|Events|act:2&shrine:No|Act 2 Events}} or {{QueryLink|Events|act:3&shrine:No|Act 3 Events}}). === Shrines === Internally, these are still called Shrines. Not to be confused with ''"events that have Shrine in their name"'' (such as {{E|Golden Shrine}}), a ''Shrine'' is a specific event type all on its own. Shrines include what a player may consider to be a "shrine", but also a few events that "might not seem like shrines". For example, {{E|Golden Shrine}} and {{E|Transmogrifier}} are shrines, but so is {{E|Wheel of Change}}. Shrines can be encountered in any Act, and can only be encountered once per Act. Once the player transitions from one Act to the next, all of the Shrines can be encountered again. For example, if the player encounters {{E|Wheel of Change}} in Act 1, it's possible for them to see it again in Act 2 and/or Act 3. Shrines are rarer than [[#Act Events|Act Events]] due to how Slay the Spire determines what event to show the player. For more information, see [[#Encountering Events|Encountering Events]]. The {{QueryLink|Events||Events List}} is currently not capable of filtering for just this specific type of event; it can only filter for the unofficial [[#Shrine Events|Shrine Events]] type which combines Shrines with [[#One-Time Events|One-Time Events]]. In the meantime, the list of Shrines is provided below for convenience. * {{E|Golden Shrine}} * {{E|Match and Keep}} * {{E|Purifier}} * {{E|Transmogrifier}} * {{E|Upgrade Shrine}} * {{E|Wheel of Change}} === One-Time Events === Internally, these are called Special One Time Events. One-Time Events can only be encountered once per run. They can each have their own Act limitations, although most One-Time Events can be encountered in any Act. For example, {{E|Bonfire Spirits}} is a One-Time Event that can be encountered in any Act. If the player encounters this event in Act 1, they will not be able to encounter it again for the rest of the run even after they transition to Act 2 or Act 3 (This is not the case for Endless Mode). One-Time Events are rarer than [[#Act Events|Act Events]] due to how Slay the Spire determines what event to show the player. For more information, see [[#Encountering Events|Encountering Events]]. This increased rarity is also what separates the One-Time Events which can only be encountered in one specific Act (such as the Act 2-exclusive {{E|N'loth}}) from the normal [[#Act Events|Act Events]]. The {{QueryLink|Events||Events List}} is currently not capable of filtering for just this specific type of event; it can only filter for the unofficial [[#Shrine Events|Shrine Events]] type which combines [[#Shrines|Shrines]] with One-Time Events. In the meantime, the list of One-Time Events is provided below for convenience. Alternatively, use the {{QueryLink|Events|shrine:Yes|Events List filtered to Shrine Events}} and disregard any of the [[#Shrines|Shrines]]. * {{E|A Note For Yourself}} * {{E|Bonfire Spirits}} * {{E|Designer In-Spire}} (only Act 2 and Act 3) * {{E|Duplicator}} * {{E|Face Trader}} (only Act 1 and Act 2) * {{E|Knowing Skull}} (only Act 2) * {{E|Lab}} * {{E|N'loth}} (only Act 2) * {{E|Ominous Forge}} * {{E|Secret Portal}} (only Act 3) * {{E|The Divine Fountain}} * {{E|The Joust}} (only Act 2) * {{E|The Woman in Blue}} * {{E|We Meet Again!}} === Shrine Events === Internally, this is not an event type at all. The Slay the Spire community tends to use the term "Shrine Events" to refer to both [[#Shrines|Shrines]] and [[#One-Time Events|One-Time Events]] as if they are a single event type. In reality, Slay the Spire keeps track of Shrines and One-Time Events in separate pools. The term to combine them likely comes from the way that Slay the Spire decides which event to present the player, since when the game determines that a rare event should be encountered it combines the pools for Shrines and the One-Time Events together and then selects a random rare event from that combined pool. For more information, see [[#Encountering Events|Encountering Events]]. For a list of all Shrine Events, see the {{QueryLink|Events|shrine:Yes|Events List filtered to Shrine Events}}. == Bugs == * [[#Shrines|Shrines]] are meant to only be encountered at most once per Act. However, there is a bug that allows them to be encountered multiple times per Act. If the player saves and quits the run in the middle of an Act, the next time they continue the run all of the [[#Shrines|Shrines]] can be encountered again even if they have already been seen before the save and quit. This is because, unlike the [[#Act Events|Act Events]] and [[#One-Time Events|One-Time Events]], the [[#Shrines|Shrine]] pool is not saved and is instead always set as if none of them have been encountered whenever an existing run is loaded. wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Face Trader | Image = Event-FaceTrader.png }} {{E|Face Trader}} is a {{QueryLink|Events|shrine:Yes|shrine Event}} found in [[Act 1]] and [[Act 2]]. This Event is the only way to obtain {{R|Cultist Headpiece}}, {{R|Face of Cleric}}, {{R|Gremlin Visage}}, {{R|N'loth's Hungry Face}}, and {{R|Ssserpent Head}}. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Touch}} {{TS|negative||Lose X HP,}} {{TS|positive||gain 75 {{Asc|15|(50)}} [[Gold]].}} * X is equal to 10% of the player's Max HP, rounded down. {{Frame|Trade}} {{TS|positive||50%: Good Face.}} {{TS|negative||50%: Bad Face.}} * Receive one of the following special [[Relics]]: ** {{R|Face of Cleric}} ({{TS|positive||good face}}) ** {{R|Ssserpent Head}} ({{TS|positive||good face}}) ** {{R|Gremlin Visage}} ({{TS|negative||bad face}}) ** {{R|N'loth's Hungry Face}} ({{TS|negative||bad face}}) ** {{R|Cultist Headpiece}} (neutral face) {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
You walk by an eerie statue holding several masks...
Something behind you softly whispers,
{{TS||up|"Stop."}}
{{Frame|Continue}}
You swerve around to face the statue which is now facing you!
On closer inspection, it's not a statue but a statuesque, gaunt man. Is he even breathing?
{{TS||up|"Face. Let me touch? Maybe trade?"}}
{{Frame|Touch}}
{{TS||up|"Compensation? Compensation."}}
Mechanically, he cranes out a neat stack of {{TS|gold||gold}} and places it in your pouch.
{{TS||up|"What a nice face. Nice face."}}
While he touches your face, you begin to feel your life drain out of it!
During this, his mask falls off and shatters. Screaming, he quickly covers his face with all six arms dropping even more masks! Amidst all the screaming and shattering, you escape.
His face was completely blank.
{{Frame|Trade}}
{{TS||up|"For me?}} {{TS||shake|FOR ME?}} {{TS||up|Oh yes.. Yes. Yes.. mmm..."}}
You see one of his arms flicker, and your face is in its hand! Your face has been swapped.
{{TS||up|"Nice face. Nice face."}}
{{Frame|Leave}}
{{TS||up|"Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop."}}
This was probably the right call.
== Notes == * The chances stated by the Event are inaccurate. The actual chances are 40% good face, 40% bad face, and 20% neutral face ({{R|Cultist Headpiece}}). ** All 5 masks have the same probability of being chosen. == Trivia == * The masks held by the Face Trader in his portrait resemble other characters seen in the game. ** From left to right, up to down: [[N'loth]], [[We Meet Again!|Ranwid]], [[The Cleric|Cleric]], the [[The Ssssserpent|Ssserpent]], [[Masked Bandits#Pointy|Pointy]], and [[Masked Bandits#Bear|Bear]]. == Update History == * '''Patch V2.0: The Watcher''' ** Face Trader event can no longer appear past Act 2. * '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion''' ** Minor text cleanup for Face Trader event. * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** Face Trader event will no longer give out duplicate relics on Endless mode. * '''Weekly Patch 33: Terror''' ** Improved Face Trader wording for top option to better reflect what happens. * '''Weekly Patch 32: Face Trader''' ** Face Trader: It's a new event! This event shows up in any Act and can give you 1 of 5 relics exclusive to this event, we think it's facetastic. ** Adding the Face Trader event. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Falling | Image = Event-Falling.png }} {{E|Falling}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 3]]. == Options == All options will randomly choose a card in the player's deck of a particular type. The option's text will explicitly tell the player which card they would lose. If the player lacks a card of a particular type, then the option relating to that type will be locked (e.g. if the player has no {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} for the {{Frame|Channel}} option, it is replaced with the option {{Frame|Locked}} Requires: Power Card).

{{Frame|Land}} {{TS|negative||Lose (a random}} ''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}''{{TS|negative||)}} * Cannot be a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} targeted by {{R|Bottled Lightning}}. {{Frame|Channel}} {{TS|negative||Lose (a random}} ''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}''{{TS|negative||)}} * Cannot be a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} targeted by {{R|Bottled Tornado}}. {{Frame|Strike}} {{TS|negative||Lose (a random}} ''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}}''{{TS|negative||)}} * Cannot be an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} targeted by {{R|Bottled Flame}}. If the player somehow manages to lack even a single eligible card (e.g. they have a very small deck containing only bottled cards), then the only option listed is a special {{Frame|Land}} option that has no description. == Dialogue ==
As you head upwards hopping from one floating shape to another, you slip
You begin to fall.

{{Frame|Continue}}

While in free fall you consider your options:
Land safely with your greatest techniques.
Channel a Power to survive the fall.
Strike at the wall to hang on to it.

{{Frame|Land}}
You land with extreme grace before continuing on.
{{Frame|Channel}}
Harnessing and expending some of your raw power, you manage to land unhurt.
{{Frame|Strike}}
You are able to latch on to the wall, and manage to make a short hop onto another stable platform.
The special {{Frame|Land}} that only occurs if the player's deck has no cards that are eligible for removal;
You seem to fall as slow as a feather, reaching the bottom without a scratch.

wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Forgotten Altar | Image = Event-ForgottenAltar.png }} {{Small Relic Infobox|Bloody Idol}} {{Small Card Infobox|Decay}} {{E|Forgotten Altar}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. This Event is the only way to obtain {{R|Bloody Idol}}. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Offer: Golden Idol}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a special}} {{R|Bloody Idol|Relic}}{{TS|positive||.}} {{TS|negative||Lose}} {{R|Golden Idol}}{{TS|negative||.}} * If the player does not have {{R|Golden Idol}}, this option is replaced with {{Frame|Locked}} Requires: Golden Idol. {{Frame|Sacrifice}} {{TS|positive||Gain 5 Max HP.}} {{TS|negative||Lose X HP.}} * X is equal to 25% {{Asc|15|(35%)}} of the player's Max HP. {{Frame|Desecrate}} {{TS|negative||Become Cursed -}}{{C|Decay}}{{TS|negative||.}} * {{C|Decay}} - {{KW|Unplayable}}. At the end of your turn, take 2 damage. == Dialogue ==
In front of you sits an altar to a forgotten god.
Atop the altar sits an ornate female statue with arms outstretched.
She calls out to you, demanding sacrifice.


{{Frame|Offer: Golden Idol}}
As you gently set the idol onto the altar a {{TS|blue||cold}} wind swirls throughout the room.
The arms of the statue begin to discolor and crumble.

Your {{TS|gold||golden idol}} begins to dull in color and begins bleeding from its eyes.
The bleeding never ceases.
{{Frame|Sacrifice}}
You stand on the altar and cut your wrists.
As the {{TS|negative||blood}} spills out in sacrifice, the arms of the statue reach out and close around your eyes.
Everything goes dark.
You wake up a short time later feeling a new potential surging through you.
{{Frame|Desecrate}}
You lash out and smash the statue in front of you, breaking the magical hold the room had placed upon you.
A dark wail echoes all around you, and you can feel the {{TS|purple|up|cursed magic}} seep into your bones.
== Notes == * {{R|Golden Idol}} is only obtained from the {{E|Golden Idol}} Event. * If the {{R|Golden Idol}} is turned into the {{R|Bloody Idol}}, {{E|The Moai Head}} Event in Act 3 will no longer accept it as an offering. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 5: Happy Holidays!''' ** Forgotten Altar now gives you the Max HP before damaging you. title: Knowing Skull
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Knowing Skull | Image = Event-KnowingSkull.png }} {{E|Knowing Skull}} is a {{QueryLink|Events|shrine:Yes|shrine Event}} found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. It will only appear if the player has at least 13 HP; guaranteeing they can select at least 1 option and leave the event without dying. == Options == The following options are presented to the player until they decide to leave the event. X is equal to 10% of the player's Max HP (minimum of 6 HP) plus the number of times they have chosen that specific option ({{TS|negative||Lose 6 HP}}, then {{TS|negative||Lose 7 HP}}, then {{TS|negative||Lose 8 HP}}, etc.)

{{Frame|A Pick Me Up?}} {{TS|positive||Get a [[Potion]].}} {{TS|negative||Lose X HP.}} * A random [[Potion]] is immediately added to the player's left-most empty potion slot. * The player is able to select this option even if all their potion slots are full or if they possess {{R|Sozu}}. They still lose HP and this option's HP loss is still increased by 1 even though no potion is obtained. {{Frame|Riches?}} {{TS|positive||Gain 90 [[Gold]].}} {{TS|negative||Lose X HP.}}

You find yourself in an old, decorated chamber. In the center of the room, a large skull sits atop an ornate pedestal. As you approach, the skull {{TS|green|shake|bursts into flames}} and turns to face you.

It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|I am War}} {{TS|negative||Fight a [[Bosses#Act 1 Bosses|Boss]] from Act 1.}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare}} [[Relic]].}} * The boss is selected at random. It can be the same boss that the player actually fought in [[Act 1]], or one of the two that they did not encounter. * In addition to the Boss dropping a {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare}} [[Relic]], it also drops normal combat rewards and 50 {{Asc|15|(25)}} [[Gold]].
{{Frame|I am Awake}} {{TS|positive||[[Upgrade]] all cards.}} {{TS|negative||You can no longer heal.}} * Obtain {{R|Mark of the Bloom}}.
{{Frame|I am Rich}} {{TS|positive||Gain 999 [[Gold]].}} {{TS|negative||Cursed - 2 {{C|Normality}}.}} * This option only appears on floors 35 to 40.
{{Frame|I am Healthy}} {{TS|positive||Heal to full HP.}} {{TS|negative||Cursed - {{C|Doubt}}.}} * This option replaces {{Frame|I am Rich}} on floor 41 and above. == Dialogue ==
While walking and traversing through the chaos of the Spire, your thoughts suddenly begin to feel very... {{TS|purple|up|real...}}

{{Frame|I am War}}

This is the way it always will be.
All will be forgotten again soon...
{{Frame|I am Rich}} or {{Frame|I am Healthy}}
Can it really be this easy?

Newly added tracks include: Mind Bloom * '''Weekly Patch 47: Metamorphosis''' ** Mind Bloom event combat now correctly gives appropriate gold for the battle. * '''Weekly Patch 43: Discovery''' ** Mind Bloom event now correctly shows curse previews for its event options. * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Adding special BGM when fighting a boss via Mind Bloom event. * '''Weekly Patch 36: Power Through''' ** Fixed an incorrect interaction with Mark of the Bloom and the Moai Head event in Act 3. * '''Weekly Patch 35: Aggregate''' ** Mind Bloom event's boss battle no longer counts as a boss for scoring or achievements. * '''Weekly Patch 29: TURBO''' ** Mind Bloom no longer shows status/curse cards upgrading. ** Mind Bloom upgrade now only shows up to 20 cards as it's CPU intensive. * '''Weekly Patch 28: The Ritual''' ** New Act 3 event: Mind Bloom ** New Relic: Mark of the Bloom {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Neow
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} [[File:Neow.png|400px|center]]{{#setmainimage:Neow.png|quiet}}Neow is a large whale-like creature with light blue skin and 6 bright yellow eyes. Neow lies at the foot of the Spire and welcomes the player at the beginning of every run. Neow blesses you based on the success of your previous run, offering [[Gold]], [[Relics]], or [[Cards]], unless you did not reach the [[Boss]] of the [[Acts#Act 1: Exordium|Exordium]], in which case she only offers two options instead of the usual four. == Shortlist (Two Blessings) Variant == If you did not reach the [[Boss]] of the [[Acts#Act 1: Exordium|Exordium]] in your last run, the Blessings she will offer are always: * Max HP +8/6/7/7 {{Asc|14|+7/5/6/6}} ([[Ironclad]] / [[Silent]] / [[Defect]] / [[Watcher]]) * {{R|Neow's Lament}}: Enemies in the next three combats will have one health. ** If the map layout allows, you can use this to get a free shot at an [[Elite]] (colloqiually called a 'snipe'). == Standard (Four Blessings) Variant == If you did reach the first boss, Neow will offer you four blessings to choose from. === First Blessing === A card-related reward from the list below: * Remove a card. * [[Transform]] a card. * [[Upgrade]] a card. * Choose a card to obtain. (''Choose one of 3 random cards of your character.'') * Choose an {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless Card}} to obtain. * Obtain a random {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare Card}}. === Second Blessing === A reward from the list below: * Max HP +8/6/7/7 {{Asc|14|+7/5/6/6}} ([[Ironclad]] / [[Silent]] / [[Defect]] / [[Watcher]]) * {{R|Neow's Lament}}: Enemies in the next three combats will have one health. * Obtain a random {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common Relic}}. * Receive 100 [[Gold]]. * Obtain 3 random [[Potions]]. === Third Blessing === A composite of a disadvantage and a more powerful reward. It can be a combination of any disadvantage and reward below, with any exceptions noted. '''Disadvantages:''' * Lose Max HP. (-8/7/7/7) {{Asc|14|(-7/6/7/6)}} ([[Ironclad]] / [[Silent]] / [[Defect]] / [[Watcher]]) * Take X damage. ** X is equal to (Current HP / 10, rounded down) * 3. ** The amount of damage is also affected by {{Asc|6|Ascension}} and {{Asc|14|Ascension}}. * Obtain a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}. * Lose all [[Gold]]. '''Advantages:''' * Remove 2 cards. ** Does not pair with '''Obtain a Curse'''. * [[Transform]] 2 cards. * Gain 250 [[Gold]]. ** Does not pair with '''Lose all Gold'''. * Choose a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare Card}} to obtain. * Choose a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless Card}} to obtain. * Obtain a random {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare Relic}}. * Gain Max HP. (+16/12/14/14) {{Asc|14|(+14/10/12/12)}} ([[Ironclad]] / [[Silent]] / [[Defect]] / [[Watcher]]) ** Does not pair with '''Lose max health''' === Fourth Blessing === * Replace your {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Starter|starter relic}} with a random {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Boss|Boss Relic}}. (''Cannot switch to the stronger version of your character's Base Relic.'') ** Commonly referred to as '''Boss Swap'''. == Lore == When choosing to '''Read''' at the Act 2 event {{E|Cursed Tome}}, you learn about the connection between [[Neow]] and the 4 playable characters.
Odd. The book seems to be about an {{TS|gold||Ancient}} named {{TS|gold||Neow.}} This piques your interest, but you have a general feeling of {{TS|purple|up|malaise.}}
The Ancient of resurrection, {{TS|gold||Neow}} was exiled to the bottom of the Spire.
You feel compelled to read more, but your body begins to {{TS|red|up|ache.}}
Seeking vengeance, {{TS|gold||Neow}} blesses outsiders, using them for her own purposes.
You are starting to feel very {{TS|red|up|weak and tired.}}
Those resurrected by {{TS|gold||Neow}} remember only fragments of their past selves, cursed to fight for eternity.
As you near the final page, your {{TS|red|shake|old wounds begin to reopen!}}
Upon finishing the tome, you decide to take it with you. With proof in hand, will you retain your memories?
 == Trivia == * After defeating the {{M|Corrupt Heart}}, an extra screen plays after the credits, depicting her saying "Has ... it ... been ... done? / The Spire sleeps ... and so shall I" * Neow is depicted as possessing powerful magical abilities, which go as far as resurrecting the dead, which she shows whenever an adventurer dies atop the Spire, so they can continue their duty. * Little is known about Neow as she is not very talkative herself. However her actions suggest that she begrudges the Spire and wants to destroy it, and does so by sending resurrected adventurers up the Spire. * The {{E|Sensory Stone}} event references the [[Defect]]'s first interaction with Neow. * Her name may be an onomatopoeia of a whale song. title: Pleading Vagrant
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Pleading Vagrant | Image = Event-Vagrant.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Shame}} {{E|Pleading Vagrant}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. It will only appear if the player has at least 75 [[Gold]]. == Options == {{Frame|Offer Gold}} {{TS|gold||85 [[Gold]]:}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a [[Relic]].}} * If the player does not have enough [[Gold]], this option will be greyed out. {{Frame|Rob}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a [[Relic]].}} {{TS|negative||Become Cursed -}} {{C|Shame}}{{TS|negative||.}}

{{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
While sneaking past a group of shrouded figures, one of them approaches you.
"Got anything for me friend? Please... maybe some {{TS|gold||Coin?"}}
"I just need somewhere to stay, I have treasures I can trade..."
He seems delusional, but harmless.


{{Frame|Offer Gold}}
"Oh yes, {{TS||up|yes!}} Here here, a fair trade!"
{{Frame|Rob}}
You snatch the precious {{TS|gold||relic}} from his clutches and walk away.
From behind you hear,
"Have you no shame? {{TS||up|HAVE YOU NO SHAAAAAME?!"}}
You have some {{TS|purple||shame.}}
{{Frame|Leave}}
(No dialogue)
== Notes == * {{R|Omamori}} can be used to prevent the {{C|Shame}} from {{Frame|Rob}} if it has any charges remaining. == Trivia == * The Pleading Vagrant Event was originally called "Addicted". It was renamed because, early into Slay the Spire's development, the vagrant previously accepted {{C|J.A.X.}} from the {{E|Augmenter}} event but was reworked to accept 85 [[Gold]] instead. Following the change, the old name no longer made sense and had to also be changed. It could have also been changed due to the negative connotations and implication of substance abuse. * Internally called Addict. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 45: Impatience''' ** Some events like Pleading Vagrant did not correctly remove remaining event choices when selecting the leave option. * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** Typo Fix on Pleading Vagrant event. * '''Weekly Patch 39: We Meet Again!''' ** Addict event reworked. ** Addicted event renamed -> Pleading Vagrant. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Scrap Ooze
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Scrap Ooze | Image = Event-ScrapOoze.png }} {{E|Scrap Ooze}} is an event found exclusively in [[Act 1]]. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Reach Inside}} {{TS|negative||Lose 3}} {{Asc|15|(5)}} {{TS|negative||HP.}} {{TS|positive||25% chance to find a [[Relic]].}} * If you fail to find a [[Relic]], you can try again until you find one. Each time you fail, the HP loss is increased by 1 and the chance to gain a Relic increases by 10%. {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Relic Distribution == * {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common Relics}} - 50% chance * {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon Relics}} - 33% chance * {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare Relics}} - 17% chance == Dialogue ==
As you walk into the room you hear a {{TS||up|gurgling}} and the {{TS||shake|grinding}} of metals. Before you is a slime-like creature that ate too much scrap for its own good. From the center of the creature you see glints of strange light, perhaps something magical? It looks like you can get some {{TS|gold||treasure}} if you just reach inside its... opening. However, the acid and sharp objects may {{TS|negative||hurt.}}
{{Frame|Reach Inside}}
Found Nothing
{{TS|negative|shake|Ouch!}}
All you find is corroded metal and a bit of {{TS|negative|shake|burning pain.}}
However, you're still convinced there's a {{TS|gold||relic...}}
Found a Relic
{{TS|positive||Success!}}
After rummaging through the metal and burning acid, you finally grab hold of a {{TS|gold||relic}} and yank it out.
You pull your way out of the ooze {{TS|negative||damaged}} but rewarded.
{{Frame|Leave}}
You decide to leave the area.
The slime pays no attention, content with its meal.

title: Secret Portal
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Secret Portal | Image = Event-SecretPortal.png }} {{E|Secret Portal}} is a shrine [[Event]] found in [[Act 3]]. It will only appear if 800 seconds (13 minutes and 20 seconds) have passed. == Options == {{Frame|Enter the Portal}} IMMEDIATELY travel to [[Bosses#Act 3 Bosses|the boss]]. * The player is put directly into combat with the [[Bosses#Act 3 Bosses|Act 3 boss]] at the end of the act.
{{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
Before you is a sight that seems out of place in the alien landscape around you. Strangely placed into one of the living walls of the Beyond is an enclosed stone entrance filled with a {{TS|purple|up|swirling magical portal.}}

You aren't sure where it leads, but maybe it could speed your journey through the Spire.
{{Frame|Enter the Portal}}
Jumping through the portal, your sense of time and space is completely torn apart.

As you reorient yourself to the new surroundings, you realize that right before you is a fearsome battle.
{{Frame|Leave}}
Careful and cautious seems the better approach for reaching the top of the Spire. Ignoring the portal you continue on.
== Notes == * Apart from the unusual method of entering the boss floor and skipping the rest of Act 3, entering the portal is otherwise a completely normal boss fight. ** {{R|Pantograph}} and {{R|Slaver's Collar}} trigger as expected. ** There will still be the {{Asc|20|double boss afterwards on A20}}. ** Defeating the boss {{Asc|20|(or both bosses)}} will still allow the player to enter [[Acts#Act 4: The Ending|Act 4]] if they have all required [[Mechanics#Keys|Keys]]. Although, the player should be careful to collect the Ruby Key from a [[Rest Site]] prior to the event since they will skip the guaranteed [[Rest Site]] before the boss (which is often relied on as the last opportunity to collect the Ruby Key). * The player's current floor is only increased by 1, which causes them to fight the [[Bosses#Act 3 Bosses|Act 3 Boss]] earlier than the usual floor 50. == Trivia == * The 800 second minimum time limit in order to encounter this event was implemented after some discussion with the Slay the Spire speedrunning community during the game's development. Without the limit, the fastest winning runs relied on encountering {{E|Secret Portal}} to skip many floors of Act 3. This would offer such an enormous time save that runs which didn't manage to find {{E|Secret Portal}} early enough could never beat runs that did. This requirement means that no speedrun would be able to encounter {{E|Secret Portal}}, while casual runs under normal gameplay would easily satisfy the minimum time requirement and be able to encounter the event as intended. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion''' ** Secret Portal event no longer says Ignored in run history. Run history rows capped at 20 elements. * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** Events: Falling, Secret Portal, Knowing Skull, Golden Idol, and Scrap Ooze receive ambient BGM. * '''Weekly Patch 18: Paranormal''' ** New Event (Beyond): Secret Portal. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Sensory Stone
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Sensory Stone | Image = Event-SensoryStone.png }} {{E|Sensory Stone}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 3]]. == Options == {{Frame|Recall}} {{TS|positive||Add 1 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card to your deck.}} {{Frame|Recall}} {{TS|positive||Add 2 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards to your deck.}} {{TS|negative||Lose 5 HP.}} {{Frame|Recall}} {{TS|positive||Add 3 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards to your deck.}} {{TS|negative||Lose 10 HP.}} == Dialogue ==
Navigating through the Beyond, you discover a {{TS|blue||glowing tesseract}} {{TS||shake|spinning}} and {{TS||up|shifting}} gently in the air.

{{Frame|Interact}}

You touch it.

A {{TS|negative|shake|sharp pain}} flows through you, followed by vivid flashes of a distant memory.
...whose memories are these?

{{Frame|Recall}} After leaving the card rewards screen, the player is presented with one of four possible dialogue texts. Each contains the memories of one of the four playable characters. The dialogue is chosen randomly, and the current character being played has no effect on which one is presented.

'''[[Ironclad]]'s Memories'''
{{TS|red|up|FEAR.}}
A demonic creature towers above you, wings spread wide as it howls with laughter. Dead bodies of a tribe surround you while the village is engulfed in terrible {{TS|purple|up|dark flames.}}
The demon calls out, taunting you.
" {{TS|red|shake|YOU REALLY ARE THE STRONGEST NOW! Haha.. HEHE... HAHAHAAAAH!!}} "
This laughter echoes forever...
'''[[Silent]]'s Memories'''
{{TS|green|up|TRIUMPH.}}
The remains of a {{TS|purple|up|ghostly creature}} sink slowly into the mud before you, barely visible in the moonlight. You have proven yourself amongst your sisters.
Standing victoriously, you wait in silence as the others ceremoniously place the {{TS|gold||creature's skull}} atop your head. The ritual has concluded.
You head towards the Spire...
'''[[Defect]]'s Memories'''
{{TS|blue|up|CONFUSION.}}
{{TS|gold||[OBJECTIVE]}} {{TS|green||BALANCE must be ENFORCED}}
{{TS|gold||[DEFINE]}} {{TS|green||BALANCE}}
{{TS|gold||[ERROR]}} {{TS|green||BALANCE NOT FOUND}}
{{TS|gold||[DEFINE]}} {{TS|green||BALANCE}}
{{TS|gold||[ERROR]}} {{TS|green||BALANCE NOT FOUND}}
{{TS|gold||[WARNING]}} {{TS|red||Large object approaching}}
{{TS||up|"I... ..am ....Neow.."}}
'''[[Watcher]]'s Memories'''
{{TS|purple|up|SERENITY.}}
Two primitive creatures fight over a carcass on the side of the road. You observe, devoid of emotion.
{{TS|gold||Watch. Remember. Live.}} This is the Watcher's mission.
Recently, one of your peers had stopped reporting on their assignment: a Spire of unknown origin.
As the fight ends, you continue onward, unfazed by the bloody scene that took place.
== Notes == * Since the {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless cards}} are actually card rewards, they are affected by [[Relics]] which modify card rewards in some way. ** {{R|Question Card}} makes each card reward present the player with 1 additional card. ** {{R|Singing Bowl}} can allow the player to skip each card reward in order to gain +2 Max HP. ** {{R|Busted Crown}} makes each card reward present the player with 2 fewer cards. ** {{R|N'loth's Gift}} increases the likelihood of each card being a {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare&color:Colorless|Rare Colorless card}}. == Trivia == * [[Ironclad]]'s {{TS|red|up|FEAR}} memory may be a reference to his {{C|Demon Form}} card as it depicts his increased power through his {{C|Burning Pact}} with a demon. ** {{KW2|Vakuu}} is most likely the demonic creature in Ironclad's memory, it possibly takes place directly after the Epoch, {{2|Timeline#Devastation|Devastation}}. * [[Silent]]'s {{TS|green|up|TRIUMPH}} memory may be a reference to her {{C|Wraith Form}} card as it depicts the end of her fight against a "ghostly creature". ** It is also likely the origin of her iconic skull mask. ** It may also reference {{M|Nemesis}}; the "ghostly creature" could match the behaviour where the monster gains {{BD|Intangible}} while fighting it. Its green rags may be somewhat reminiscent of the cloak that [[Silent]] wears as well. "Nemesis" is also a somewhat odd name for a monster as a "nemesis" can also be interpreted as an "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archenemy archenemy]"; the main enemy of a protagonist. * [[Defect]]'s {{TS|blue|up|CONFUSION}} memory may be a reference to its self-aware nature, perhaps triggered by its inability to define or understand "balance", before being found by [[Neow]]. * [[Watcher]]'s {{TS|purple|up|SERENITY}} memory may be a reference to {{E|The Joust}} as she watches two knights fight over the remains of "Noodles"; the former pet of one of the knights. ** It is also [[Time Eater#Trivia|one of the hints]] that may indicate that {{M|Time Eater}} used to belong to Watcher's order as it is possible that they were the peer who entered the Spire and never returned. == Update History == * '''Patch V2.0: The Watcher''' ** ''NOTE: There are no official patch notes for this change, but the Sensory Stone event gained its fourth dialogue option memory for the Watcher.'' * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Adding ambient SFX for Sensory Stone event. * '''Weekly Patch 29: TURBO''' ** Fix grammar issue in Sensory Stone event. * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** Additional lore in the Sensory Stone event. ** Egg relics now show pre-upgraded cards for Sensory Stone event's choices. * '''Weekly Patch 21: Channel Lightning''' ** Sensory Stone event wording fix. * '''Weekly Patch 20: Immolate''' ** Wording fixes in Sensory Stone event. * '''Weekly Patch 19: Seed''' ** Grammar improvements for Sensory Stone event. * '''Weekly Patch 18: Paranormal''' ** Hotfix: Fixed issue where Sensory Stone event may give you colored cards. ** New Event (Beyond): Sensory Stone. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: The Cleric
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = The Cleric | Image = Event-Cleric.png }} {{E|The Cleric}} is a {{QueryLink|Events|shrine:Yes|shrine Event}} found exclusively in [[Act 1]]. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. It can only be encountered if the player has at least 35 [[Gold]]; enough to afford at least one of the options. == Options == {{Frame|Heal}} {{TS|gold||35 [[Gold]]:}} {{TS|positive||Heal X HP.}} * X is equal to 25% of the player's Max HP, rounded down. {{Frame|Purify}} {{TS|gold||50}} {{Asc|15|(75)}} {{TS|gold||[[Gold]]:}} {{TS|positive||Remove a card from your deck.}} {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
A strange blue humanoid with a golden helm(?) approaches you with a huge smile. {{TS||shake|"Hello friend!}} I am {{TS|blue||Cleric!}} Are you interested in my services?!" the creature shouts, loudly. {{Frame|Heal}}
A warm golden light envelops your body and dissipates. The creature grins. "Cleric best healer. {{TS||shake|Have a good day!"}}
{{Frame|Purify}}
A cold blue flame envelops your body and dissipates. The creature grins. "Cleric talented. {{TS||shake|Have a good day!"}}
{{Frame|Leave}}
You don't trust this {{TS|blue||"Cleric",}} so you leave.
== Trivia == * Cleric is also encountered in the {{E|Old Beggar}} event. * {{R|Face of Cleric}} from the {{E|Face Trader}} event references Cleric. title: The Colosseum
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = The Colosseum | Image = Event-Colosseum.png }} {{E|The Colosseum}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. It only appears after the guaranteed [[Map Locations#Treasure Room|Treasure Room]] on the 6th floor. == Options == {{Frame|Fight}} * The player enters a fight with a {{M|Blue Slaver}} and {{M|Red Slaver}}. This fight gives no rewards.
After the fight ends, a choice has to be made: {{Frame|COWARDICE}} Escape.

{{Frame|VICTORY}} A powerful fight with many rewards. * The player enters a fight with {{M|Taskmaster}} and {{M|Gremlin Nob}}. * The rewards are 100 [[Gold]], 1 {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare}} [[Relic]], 1 {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} [[Relic]], a card reward, and sometimes a [[Potion]].
== Dialogue ==
{{TS||shake|Thwack!!!}}
..
......
...
{{TS||up|You were knocked unconscious...}}


{{Frame|Continue}}

{{TS||up|Groggy}} and with a {{TS||shake|throbbing}} head, you awaken to find yourself thrown in the center of a massive stadium with an overflowing audience of {{TS|blue||Slavers,}} {{TS|purple||Cultists,}} and other denizens of the City!
An armored giant with a {{TS|gold||golden crown}} bellows at you from atop,
{{TS||shake|"WE NOW BEGIN THE 4200TH COMBAT!!!!"}}
A gate on the opposite side opens...
{{Frame|Fight}}
(The player enters combat with a {{M|Blue Slaver}} and {{M|Red Slaver}}. After ending the fight, more dialogue is presented.)

{{TS||shake|"WELL DONE, WEAKLING!"}}
The giant mock claps whilst he riles up the crowd with exaggerated gestures.
{{TS|gold|up|Gold}} {{TS||up|and}} {{TS|gold|up|confetti}} {{TS||up|shower you!}}
{{TS||shake|"TIME FOR THE REAL CHALLENGE!!"}}

The last battle left a small hole in the Colosseum's wall, you can easily escape through there while everyone is distracted.
Do you stay and fight?
{{Frame|COWARDICE}}
(No dialogue)
{{Frame|VICTORY}}
(No dialogue, the player enters combat with {{M|Taskmaster}} and {{M|Gremlin Nob}})
== Notes == Some mechanics behave strangely during the two fights in this event due to their atypical nature: * {{Frame|Fight}} is treated as a normal combat. ** {{P|Smoke Bomb}} can be used to escape the fight and the player will still be prompted to choose either {{Frame|COWARDICE}} or {{Frame|VICTORY}} afterwards as normal. ** The game still rolls to drop a [[Potion]], but never presents the player with it even if a [[Potion]] would be dropped. This means it is impossible to know if the [[Potions#Sources|potion chance]] has increased or decreased, and this uncertainty will persist until the [[Potions#Sources|potion chance]] resets at start of the next act. ** While it has no combat rewards and transitions to the next dialogue of the event very quickly, end-of-combat effects like {{R|Burning Blood}} and {{C|Self Repair}} will still trigger. * {{Frame|VICTORY}} is treated as an [[Elite]] combat for ''most'' effects. ** {{R|Preserved Insect}}, {{R|Sling of Courage}}, and {{R|Slaver's Collar}} will all trigger their effects as expected. ** The only exception is {{R|Black Star}}, which has no effect on the [[Relics]] dropped as rewards. This combat will ''always'' drop exactly 1 {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Rare|Rare}} [[Relic]] and 1 {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} [[Relic]]. == Trivia == * The "armored giant with a {{TS|gold||golden crown}}" is likely {{M|The Champ}}. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** Colosseum event now appears only at the top half of Act 2. * '''Slay the Spire 1.0: Farewell Early Access''' ** Colossuem Nob fight ordering swapped so that the Nob can apply Vulnerable. * '''Weekly Patch 56: The Collector''' ** Colosseum event's second fight is now a Gremlin Nob + Taskmaster (rather than 2 Gremlin Nobs) * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Orb VFX no longer render in the background of the Colosseum event. * '''Weekly Patch 41: Chill''' ** Colosseum Nobs no longer play double music. ** Fixed bug causing block to maintain between colosseum combats. ** Fixed Smoke Bomb and Colosseum bug that caused the player to go invisible. ** Killing a Colosseum Nob no longer causes the music to stop. * '''Weekly Patch 39: We Meet Again!''' ** Added City Event: The Colosseum. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: The Joust
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = The Joust | Image = Event-Joust.png }} {{E|The Joust}} is a shrine [[Event]] found in [[Act 2]]. This event can only be encountered with more than 50 [[Gold]]. == Options == {{Frame|Murderer}} {{TS|gold||Bet 50 Gold}} - {{TS|positive||70%: win 100 Gold.}} {{Frame|Owner}} {{TS|gold||Bet 50 Gold}} - {{TS|positive||30%: win 250 Gold.}} There is no option to avoid betting. == Dialogue ==
As you make your way through the large buildings you come across a long narrow bridge and spot knights on either side, facing one another.
You approach...
{{TS||shake|"HALT!"}}
A knight forcefully gestures you to stop with its giant lance.


{{Frame|Continue}}
"Today is the day I must settle the score with the {{TS|negative||murderer}} of my beloved pet, {{TS|gold||Noodles.}} Until then, you may not pass.
Fellow witness, why don't you {{TS|blue||bet}} on who you think will emerge victorious?"
{{Frame|Murderer}}
"I can't believe you're betting against {{TS|gold||Noodles!"}}
Furious, he clamps down his helmet and rushes towards his nemesis.
{{Frame|Owner}}
"Give me strength, {{TS|gold||Noodles!"}}
Clamping down his helmet, the knight charges forward.
{{TS|gold|shake|* CRASH!!!* }} {{TS|negative|shake|* KLAAAANG!* }}
{{TS|green|shake|* POW!* }}
'''Depending on who loses the joust:''' The owner died. / The nemesis was slain.

'''When losing the bet:'''
You {{TS|negative||lost}} the bet, but at least you weren't gouged by a lance.
'''When winning the bet:'''
You {{TS|green||win}} the bet. Unsure what to think, you grab your winnings and leave.
== Notes == * If the player possesses {{R|Ectoplasm}}, this event is a mandatory loss of 50 [[Gold]]. There is no option to leave the event without betting, and any potential winnings cannot be gained. * The player may consider using the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value expected value] (EV) of each option to determine who they want to bet on. ** The EV of betting on the Murderer is a net increase of 20 [[Gold]] (a 70% chance to receive 100 [[Gold]] is an expected 70 [[Gold]], minus the 50 [[Gold]] that was bet. 0.7 x 100 - 50 = 20) ** The EV of betting on the Owner is a net increase of 25 [[Gold]] (a 30% chance to receive 250 [[Gold]] is an expected 75 [[Gold]], minus the 50 [[Gold]] that was bet. 0.3 x 250 - 50 = 25) ** It may be more beneficial to ignore the EV and instead consider whether the relatively safe 50 extra [[Gold]] by betting on the Murderer is more useful to the player's current run compared to risking the bet on the Owner and likely losing their 50 [[Gold]] for the more unlikely net gain of 200 [[Gold]]. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 21: Channel Lightning''' ** Seeds are now utilized for The Joust event. * '''Weekly Patch 2: Slimes!''' ** Joust event now has correct wording for some incorrect options. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: The Library
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = The Library | Image = Event-Library.png }} {{E|The Library}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Read}} {{TS|positive||Choose 1 of 20 cards to add to your deck.}}

{{Frame|Sleep}} {{TS|positive||Heal X HP.}} * X is equal to 33% {{Asc|15|(20%)}} of the player's Max HP. == Dialogue ==
You come across an ornate building which appears abandoned.
A plaque that has been torn free from a wall is on the floor. It reads, {{TS|blue||"THE LIBRARY".}}
Inside, you find countless rows of scrolls, manuscripts, and books.
You pick one and cozy yourself into a chair for some quiet time.

{{Frame|Read}} There are 3 possible stories that the player can read. One of the following is chosen at random.
The story is about an insect-controlling teenage girl who aspires to become a hero. The book is filled with creative uses of power, combat strategies, and varying perspectives.

Satisfying.
The story is about a man who journeyed beyond the stars and found himself stuck on a desolate foreign planet. Ingenuity, luck, perseverance, and humor to retain his sanity were his tools to return home.

Fascinating.
The story takes place in a giant isolated building underground as the outside conditions have become unbearable. The novel is mired with conspiracies, propaganda, and injustice. You ponder if similar dynamics are at play within the Spire.

Unsettling.
{{Frame|Sleep}}
Reading is for chumps.
You doze off in a comfy chair instead.
{{TS||up|Zzz... zzz... ..Zz...}}
You wake up feeling refreshed.
== Notes == * {{Frame|Sleep}} is unaffected by {{R|Regal Pillow}}, does not trigger {{R|Dream Catcher}}, and can still be chosen with {{R|Coffee Dripper}}. * {{R|Mark of the Bloom}} makes {{Frame|Sleep}} serve only as a way to skip adding a card to your deck as it will no longer heal you. * {{R|N'loth's Gift}} increases the likelihood of each card offered by {{Frame|Read}} being {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}}. == Trivia == * Each of the stories that can be randomly chosen when {{Frame|Read}} is selected are references to real-world books. They are: ** [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worm_(web_serial) Worm, by John C. McCrae]. Referenced by the story about the ''"insect-controlling teenage girl"''. ** [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Martian_(Weir_novel) The Martian, by Andy Weir]. Referenced by the story about the ''"man who journeyed beyond the stars"''. ** [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silo_(series) Wool, by Hugh Howey]. Referenced by the story about the ''"giant isolated building underground"''. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** Library event can no longer contain duplicate cards. * '''Weekly Patch 53: Blizzard''' ** Fix for Egg relics causing an issue with cards in the Library event screen. * '''Weekly Patch 18: Paranormal''' ** Fix for Calling Bell/Library/Pandora's Box exploit. * '''Weekly Patch 16: Back to Work''' ** You can now view your deck or the map when the grid card select screen is up (Such as The Library event) * '''Weekly Patch 5: Happy Holidays!''' ** Insect-controlling -> typo in The Library event's text. * '''Weekly Patch 2: Slimes!''' ** Updating The Library event's option to clarify that you choose 1 of 20 cards rather than the usual 3. * '''Day 1 Patch''' ** Minor wording updates for Library event. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. == Options == {{Frame|Open Coffin}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a [[Relic]].}} {{TS|negative||50% {{Asc|15|(100%)}}: Become Cursed - {{C|Writhe}}}} {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
Venturing through a series of tombs, you are faced with a large sarcophagus {{TS||up|studded with gems}} in the center of a circular room.
You cannot make out the writing on the coffin, however, you do notice {{TS|purple|up|black fog}} seeping out from the sides.


{{Frame|Open Coffin}} The dialogue changes depending on whether the player becomes cursed with {{C|Writhe}} or not. '''If the player does not receive {{C|Writhe}}:'''
You push open the coffin. The fog dissipates harmlessly. Inside, you find the mortal remains of a decorated soldier grasping an old {{TS|gold||relic.}} You pilfer it and move on.

title: The Moai Head
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = The Moai Head | Image = Event-MoaiHead.png }} {{Small Relic Infobox|Golden Idol}} {{E|The Moai Head}} is an [[Event]] found in [[Act 3]]. It is one of the events affected by {{Asc|15|Ascension}}. It can only be encountered if the player either has {{R|Golden Idol}}, or their HP is at or below 50%. == Options == {{Frame|Jump Inside}} {{TS|positive||Heal to full HP.}} {{TS|negative||Lose X Max HP.}} * X is equal to 12.5% {{Asc|15|(18%)}} of the player's Max HP. {{Frame|Offer: {{R|Golden Idol}}}} {{TS|positive||Receive 333 [[Gold]].}} {{TS|negative||Lose {{R|Golden Idol}}.}} * If the player lacks {{R|Golden Idol}}, this option is replaced with {{Frame|Locked}} Requires: {{R|Golden Idol}}. {{Frame|Leave}} Nothing happens.

== Dialogue ==
You stumble across something that feels * very* out of place. Before you, an enormous stony head emerges from a large wall segment that does not shift and change like the rest of this area.
The head's mouth is wide open, and it reveals large intimidating teeth stained red with blood. The surface of the status is riddled with pictographs that seem to indicate people throwing themselves into the mouth of this head and being devoured. Why would anyone do that?
{{Frame|Jump Inside}}
At first when you step into the mouth of the statue, nothing happens.
As you start to feel more than a little foolish, the huge molars slam down from above, crushing you whole.
{{TS||shake|Darkness.}}
Sometime later from within the dark, you see a sliver of light, and hear what you now realize is the sound of stony teeth slowly rising upwards.


You leave confused.
{{Frame|Offer: {{R|Golden Idol}}}}
You jump back a little as the gigantic molars smash down on the idol, smashing it to dust. As the teeth start to rise up again, {{TS|gold||gold}} pours forth in a torrent from the opening, flooding you with riches.
{{Frame|Leave}}
You leave, wondering what could have been.
== Notes == * {{R|Golden Idol}} is acquired from the [[Act 1]] event of the same name; {{E|Golden Idol}}. * {{E|The Moai Head}} is the last opportunity to trade the {{R|Golden Idol}}, the other being the {{E|Forgotten Altar}} event in [[Act 2]]. * The 333 [[Gold]] from {{Frame|Offer: Golden Idol}} easily outperforms any remaining [[Gold]] the player could gain from combats by keeping the {{R|Golden Idol}}, especially since they likely do not have many combats left in the run by the time they reach this [[Act 3]] event. * The healing from {{Frame|Jump Inside}} will be prevented if the player has {{R|Mark of the Bloom}}. == Trivia == * The real world [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moai Moai] are a set of stone human-like statues constructed by the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapa_Nui_people Rapa Nui people] on [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Island Rapa Nui (commonly known as Easter Island)]. * This event may be a reference to the [https://spelunky.fandom.com/wiki/Moai_(HD) Moai from Spelunky], where they are a key component in accessing the City of Gold by entering the Moai's mouth. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 36: Power Through''' ** Fixed an incorrect interaction with the Mark of the Bloom and the Moai Head event in Act 3. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Vampires
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Vampires | Image = Event-Vampires.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Bite}} {{Small Relic Infobox|Blood Vial}} {{E|Vampires}} is an [[Event]] found exclusively in [[Act 2]]. == Options == {{Frame|Offer: Blood Vial}} {{TS|negative||Lose}} {{R|Blood Vial}}{{TS|negative||.}} Remove all {{C|Strike (Ironclad)|Strikes}}{{TS|positive||.}} Receive 5 {{C|Bite|Bites}}{{TS|positive||.}} * Only present if the player has {{R|Blood Vial}}. {{Frame|Accept}} Remove all {{C|Strike (Ironclad)|Strikes}}{{TS|positive||.}} Receive 5 {{C|Bite|Bites}}{{TS|positive||.}} Lose X Max HP. * X is equal to 30% of the player's max HP. {{Frame|Refuse}} Nothing happens. You are then given the option to {{Frame|Leave}}. == Dialogue ==
Navigating an unlit street, you come across several hooded figures in the midst of some dark ritual. As you approach, they turn to you in eerie unison. The tallest among them bares fanged teeth and extends a long, pale hand towards you.
{{TS||up|"Join us brother, and feel the warmth of the Spire."}}


{{Frame|Offer: Blood Vial}}
The pale figures gasp as you take out the {{TS|gold||Blood Vial.}}
{{TS||up|"The master's blood... the master's blood!}} {{TS||shake|THE MASTER'S BLOOD!"}}
They all chant fervently as the tall one bows before you. "Drink from His blood, and become one with {{TS|gold|up|Him."}}
The chant growing louder, you consume the contents of the vial. Your vision immediately {{TS||up|warps}} and fades to darkness.

You wake up some time later, alone. An intense {{TS||up|hunger}} passes through your belly. You {{TS|red||must feed...}}
{{Frame|Accept}}
The tall figure grabs your arm, pulls you forward, and sinks his fangs into your neck. You feel a {{TS||shake|dark force}} pour into your neck and {{TS||shake|course}} through your body.
...
You wake up some time later, alone. An intense {{TS||up|hunger}} passes through your belly. You {{TS|red||must feed...}}
{{Frame|Refuse}}
You step back and raise your weapon in defiance. The tall figure sighs.
"Very well." The entire group of hooded figures morph into a thick black fog that flows away from you.
You are alone once more.
== Trivia == * The ''{{TS||up|"Join us"}}'' line of dialogue changes depending on the player's current character. ** For the [[Ironclad]] it reads, ''{{TS||up|"Join us brother"}}''. ** For the [[Silent]] and the [[Watcher]] it reads, ''{{TS||up|"Join us sister"}}''. ** For the [[Defect]] it reads, ''{{TS||up|"Join us broken one"}}''. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** Vampires and Council of Ghosts events now show how much Max HP is lost (rather than showing %) * '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion''' ** Minor text cleanup for Vampires event. * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** When accepting to become a vampire, a SFX now plays. * '''Weekly Patch 30: Skewer''' ** Fix for Vampire and Ghost Council event which could set your HP to 0. * '''Weekly Patch 5: Happy Holidays!''' ** Vampires event dialog option is slightly shortened so it fits in the option. * '''Weekly Patch 1: The First of Many!''' ** Vampires event text now displays the correct options if you reject them. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: We Meet Again!
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = We Meet Again! | Image = Event-WeMeetAgain.png }} {{E|We Meet Again!}} is a shrine [[Event]] found in all [[Acts]]. Shrine events appear less frequently than other events. == Options == {{Frame|Give Potion}} {{TS|negative||Lose a chosen potion.}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a Relic.}} * The event will randomly choose a potion upon entry and tell you which one was selected. You will be unable to drink or discard that potion until you leave the event's floor. {{Frame|Give Gold}} {{TS|negative||Lose Gold.}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a Relic.}} * The amount of [[Gold]] lost is between 50 and 150 (or your current amount of [[Gold]]). {{Frame|Give Card}} {{TS|negative||Lose a chosen card.}} {{TS|positive||Obtain a Relic.}} * The chosen card will not be {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} or a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}. {{Frame|Attack}} Nothing happens. == Dialogue ==
"We meet again!"
A cheery disheveled fellow approaches you gleefully. You do not know this man.
"It's me! {{TS|gold||Ranwid!}} Have any goods for me today? The usual? A fella like me can't make it alone, you know?"
You eye him suspiciously and consider your options.
{{Frame|Give Potion}}
"Exquisite! Was feeling parched."
{{TS|blue|up|Glup glup glup}}
He downs the potion in one go and lets out a satisfied {{TS||shake|burp.}}
{{Frame|Give Gold}}
"Magnificent! This will be quite handy if I run into those {{TS|red||mask wearing hoodlums}} again."
{{Frame|Give Card}}
"Exemplary! I shall study this further in my chambers."
He rummages around in his various pockets...
"Here, look what I've got for you today! Take it take it!"
{{Frame|Attack}}
"{{TS||shake|Aaaaagghh!!}} What a jerk you are sometimes!"
He runs away.
== Notes == * "{{TS|red||mask wearing hoodlums}}" likely refers to the group of bandits in the Act 2 event {{E|Masked Bandits}}. {{EventNav}} [[Category:Events]]

title: Wheel of Change
wikitext:
{{Event Infobox | Name = Wheel of Change | Image = Event-SpinTheWheel.png }} {{E|Wheel of Change}} is a shrine [[Event]] found in all [[Acts]]. Shrine events appear less frequently than other acts. {{Clear}} == Options ==
[[File:SpinButton.png|100px|thumb|Spin Button.]] [[File:WheelArrow.png|100px|thumb|Wheel arrow.]] [[File:Wheel.png|250px|thumb|Wheel.]]
{{Frame|Play}} * Spin a wheel containing the following "prizes" (clockwise starting at 12 o'clock in the image): ** Take 10% ({{Asc|15|15%}}) of your Max HP as damage. ** Gain [[Gold]] ** Gain a random [[Relic]] ** Heal to full HP ** Become Cursed - {{C|Decay}} ** Remove a card from your deck. {{Clear}} == Dialogue ==
You come upon a dapper looking, cheery gremlin.
"It's time to spin the wheel! Are you {{TS||up|R E A D Y ?}} Of course you are!"
When receiving a [[Relic]]
"Ah, a {{TS|green||gift!}}
Enjoy!"
When taking damage
"Uh oh!
You lose!"
You spot him readying a shiv...
You slash at the crazy gremlin but he's simply too quick!
He gets you a few times with a crude shiv.
"The price has been paid!!"
and with that, both the gremlin and its wheel disappear in a puff of smoke.
When obtaining [[Gold]]
"You win some {{TS|gold||GOLD!}}
YAY!!!!"
When obtaining {{C|Decay}}
"Looks like you won a {{TS|purple||Curse!}}
That's not good.
Oh well! Better luck next time!"
When removing a card from your deck
"Ohh, the power of {{TS|negative|up|darkness...}}
Choose a card to remove from your deck!"
